title: Share Trading Policy

tiers.name: Directors, officers and employees
tiers.description: All directors, officers and employees of the Company; subject to the General Policy (no dealing while in possession of price sensitive information, no procuring others to deal, 12-month short-term trading ban, 4-week blackout before results/AGM, post-trade notification to the Company Secretary within 2 working days).

tiers.name: Restricted persons
tiers.description: Directors of the Company, all executives reporting directly to the Managing Director, and any other employees considered appropriate by the Managing Director from time to time; may only deal during defined window periods (and only after checking with the Chairman or Managing Director), or in a closed period with prior written approval in exceptional circumstances.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: A director of the Company (a Restricted person); must check with the Chairman before dealing in a window period, and must inform and secure the Chairman's written approval to deal in a closed period.

tiers.name: Chairman
tiers.description: The Chairman of the Company (a Restricted person); must inform and secure written approval from the remainder of the Board to deal in a closed period.

tiers.name: Executives
tiers.description: An executive reporting directly to the Managing Director, or other employee designated by the Managing Director (a Restricted person); must check with the Managing Director before dealing in a window period, and must inform and secure the Managing Director's written approval to deal in a closed period.

rules.detail: The policy's concept of trading is defined narrowly: shares plus 'other securities issued by the Company including options'. A third-party OTC put/call written by a bank over the Company's shares is not a security issued by the Company and is not otherwise mentioned, so it falls outside the policy's express scope (subject to the freestanding LTIP hedging ban in clause 5.1.2).
rules.evidence: For the purposes of this policy, trading in the Company's shares also extends to trading in other securities issued by the Company including options.

rules.detail: LTIP participants are banned from any scheme protecting value or locking in price of unexercised/unawarded options or shares.
rules.evidence: Participants are prohibited from entering into any scheme or arrangement to protect the value or lock in a price of those options or shares before the exercise or award date.

rules.detail: The clause 5.1.2 hedging ban is expressly time-limited to 'before the exercise or award date'; once shares vest and are held outright, no hedging restriction is stated, and hedging via a third-party OTC derivative would not be 'trading in the Company's shares' under the policy's narrow definition.
Prepaid forwards or other monetisation structures are not mentioned.
CFDs are not mentioned and, like other third-party derivatives, are not 'securities issued by the Company'.
Margin lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
Granting security, a charge, lien or pledge over shares is not mentioned.
No secured financing or collateral arrangement of any kind is addressed.
Buying and selling the same parcel of shares (or part) within a twelve month period is banned; softer aspirational guidance in 3.1 also discourages short-term or speculative trading generally.
rules.evidence: Directors, officers and employees must not engage in short term trading i.e. the buying and selling of the same parcel of shares (or part thereof) within a twelve month period.

exceptions.evidence: Exceptional Circumstances – prior written approval for trading during closed period may be granted where severe financial circumstances arise which cannot be resolved other than by selling the company's shares.

Where the Company operates dividend reinvestment plans, share buy-back schemes or equity issues, as determined by the Company's Board of Directors, these company initiated actions will be subject to the relevant legal requirements and will operate separate from, and not be subject to, this Share Trading Policy.

exemption_authority: Chairman, remainder of the Board, or Managing Director (as applicable under 4.2.4) may grant prior written approval to trade during a closed period only in exceptional circumstances/severe financial hardship (4.2.5) where satisfied no price sensitive information exists; no other waiver mechanism is stated.

bespoke_clauses.clause: trading in the Company's shares also extends to trading in other securities issued by the Company including options
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy's coverage is limited to shares and Company-issued options; a bank's OTC put/call and its secured loan are not securities issued by the Company and are not otherwise mentioned, so they likely sit entirely outside the express Share Trading Policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Participants are prohibited from entering into any scheme or arrangement to protect the value or lock in a price of those options or shares before the exercise or award date.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only express hedging restriction ends at exercise/award, so a collar over already-vested shares is not caught by this clause.

bespoke_clauses.clause: (no clause addresses margin lending, secured financing, encumbrance, charges, liens or pledges)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no policy-based obstacle to pledging vested shares to secure the bank's loan, though the director's own duties, general law and ASX Listing Rule disclosure of security interests over director-held securities remain separately relevant.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the takeover provisions which restrict dealings in Company securities when their combined shareholding interest exceeds 20%
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cash-settled collar should not itself create a relevant interest, but a physically-settled structure or security interest granted to the bank should be checked against this 20% threshold.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors, officers and employees must advise the Company Secretary in writing of the details of any completed transactions within 2 working days of the transaction.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If entry into, or unwind/settlement of, the collar is treated as 'trading in the Company's shares', it must be disclosed to the Company Secretary within 2 working days regardless of tier.

summary: On this policy's own terms, 'trading in the Company's shares' extends only to shares and options issued by the Company itself, so a bank-written OTC put and call and a loan secured on the collared shares are not squarely covered — the policy is silent on margin lending, secured financing, encumbrance, CFDs and third-party derivatives generally. The one express hedging restriction (clause 5.1.2) bars LTIP participants only from protecting value or locking in a price of options or shares 'before the exercise or award date', so it does not reach already-vested, unrestricted shares. To the extent the collar or its unwind is nonetheless treated as 'trading in the Company's shares', Restricted Persons (directors, direct reports to the Managing Director, and other designated employees) may only deal in defined post-results/AGM window periods after checking with the Chairman or Managing Director, or in a closed period with written Board/Chairman/MD approval limited to severe financial hardship, and never while holding inside information; all directors, officers and employees also face a 12-month same-parcel short-term trading ban, a 4-week blackout before results and the AGM, and must notify the Company Secretary of completed transactions within 2 working days. A funded collar over vested shares is therefore more readily available under this document than under a typical modern policy, provided dealing occurs outside blackout periods and (for Restricted Persons) with the requisite Chairman/MD sign-off, but this favourable reading rests on a narrow, dated (2010) definition that the Company could interpret more broadly if asked directly.
